title: Quiet Please
paragraphs: Wyllis Cooper’s atmospheric anthology, usually narrated by Ernest Chappell, blends supernatural suspense, horror, fantasy, and psychological drama.

Wyllis Cooper atmospheric anthology built around original radio scripts, frequently first-person narration by featured actor Ernest Chappell, blending supernatural suspense, fantasy, horror and psychological drama.

GRH documents the program through Mutual era (June 8, 1947 to September 13, 1948) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] and ABC era (September 19, 1948 to June 25, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Ernest Chappell (performer on 71 recordings), Wyllis Cooper (director on 70 recordings, writer on 70 recordings, host on 69 recordings, and producer on 1 recording), Albert Buhrman (organist on 62 recordings), Pat O'Malley (performer on 15 recordings), Gene Parazzo (organist on 9 recordings), Ed Latimer (performer on 7 recordings), and Lotte Stavisky (performer on 7 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.e3a6b5feab2dd0c5|WJZ]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include death and mortality, supernatural and uncanny phenomena, time and temporal dislocation, war and military aftermath, ghosts and the dead, and memory and identity.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Original writing for the radio medium, Mutual-to-ABC network transition, and Wyllis Cooper horror-radio lineage.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (18 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (20 shared credited people), [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (17 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (15 shared credited people), and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (14 shared credited people).
